title_as_printed: The Value of Handgrip Strength and Self-Rated Squat Ability in Predicting Mild Cognitive Impairment: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model
blind_code_notes: Category: C4 arguable as a secondary domain for dynamometer-measured handgrip strength.

Task_Type.reason: Multivariable logistic regression models discriminate current MCI (education-adjusted MMSE cut-offs) from non-MCI older adults, with AUC reported.
Task_Type.quote: The 3 models all yielded good discrimination performance (area under the curve values ranged from 0.719 to 0.732).

Category.reason: Population survey data (sociodemographic, behavioural, PHQ-9, Barthel ADL, chronic conditions, self-rated squat ability) plus measured handgrip strength; primary domain is clinical/population (C5).
Category.quote: Data from the Anhui Province Healthy Longevity Survey (AHLS) were extracted for analysis in the current study.

Validation_Type.reason: Random 7:3 development/validation split of one survey (no external site), with 10-fold CV inside the development set as a sensitivity analysis.
Validation_Type.quote: We divided the original set into a development set and a validation set at a ratio of 7:3

Sample_N_Approx.quote: Finally, 5393 participants were included in the analysis

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Chinese community survey (AHLS); no ADNI data.

notes: Row agrees with the PDF on all six fields.
